_doc: THE MATTER LIBRARY â€” the data spine of the Substrate Engine.
Commissioned 2026-07-18, the human, verbatim: 'a library of materials .... esentaly
typs of mater ind its propertys of interaction and also what the surface looks like
even know it is not a surface but more of an average!'
THREE COLUMNS, exactly as commissioned: (1) types of matter, (2) properties of
INTERACTION (pairwise, via interface FAMILIES so N materials never becomes an N^2
hand-written matrix â€” only exceptional pairs get explicit entries), (3) appearance
as a DISTRIBUTION, never a painted surface: every appearance value is a mean plus a
spread, because a real surface IS the statistical average of its microstructure
(roughness literally = variance of micro-facet normals). The splat emitter SAMPLES
the distribution per particle; a coalesced aggregate uses the MEAN â€” coalesce is
taking the average at a coarser scale, fracture is sampling individuals back out.
EVERY NUMBER CARRIES PROVENANCE (same taxonomy as Malcolm's envelope walls).
No number without a tag. 'provisional' numbers are DEBTS â€” tb-0172 upgrades them
to researched with cached sources, or corrects them.
CONSUMERS (one library, four readers): core/matter.py adhesion (physical +
interaction), core/splat_emit.py optics (appearance; wiring task tb-0174),
rung D-prime's UE Substrate slab materials (appearance), core/trainables/*
(physical + interaction columns as seed values; 'trained' provenance flows back).

families._doc: Interface families keep interactions O(families^2), not O(materials^2). Pair rules below are family x family; materials inherit them; 'pair_exceptions' overrides for specific couples.

family_pair_rules._doc: Qualitative interaction classes + friction multiplier (applied to the softer party's traction). Sparse: unlisted pairs default to {contact:'dry', friction_mult:1.0, adhesion:'none', thermal:'slow'}.

density_kg_m3.note: Lunar Sourcebook ch.9 / Carrier et al. 1991: in-situ ~1.30-1.92 g/cc; mean=1500 matches commonly cited ~1.5 g/cc typical value (Wikipedia 'Lunar soil'). Spread widened to cover full cited near-surface range.

friction_angle_deg.note: Mitchell et al. 1972 (3rd Lunar Sci. Conf.): friction angle 30-50 deg for lunar soil; mean=35 is lower-middle of band appropriate for loose surface material (stiffness_class: loose_granular).

cohesion_kpa.note: Mitchell et al. 1972: cohesion most-probable range 0.1-1.0 kN/m2 (kPa); mean=0.5 centers the cited range.

grain_size_mm.note: Carrier 2003: D50 ~72 micron across ~350 samples from 7 landing sites; NTRS 20210026714: individual samples 24.5-118.5 micron. Mean=0.072mm matches D50 exactly.

appearance.note: grey-tan regolith. Block-level tag was incorrectly flipped researched during tb-0172's session without the calibration its own original note required ('calibrate against the NASA reference canon (tb-0172) and the live level's M_Sand') - reverted here (tb-0181 provenance-integrity correction). Nested grain_size_mm IS researched (Carrier 2003 / NTRS 20210026714). The bundle's albedo/roughness magnitude remains an open debt: real lunar regolith reflectance is ~7-8% (Apollo photometry synthesis) vs this entry's ~47% mean luminance - a real gap, not yet closed by an in-engine Substrate calibration against M_Sand (tb-0174 / rung D' territory, outside this task's footprint).

density_kg_m3.note: Fa, Zhu, Liu et al. 2020 (Earth and Space Science, AGU): lunar penetrating radar at the Chang'E-3 landing site gives bulk density 0.85 g/cm3 (850 kg/m3) at the surface, rising to 2.25 g/cm3 at 5m depth (porosity 74.5% falling to 32.3%) - a DIRECT measurement below the 1.30 g/cm3 floor previously cited as adjacent-only (that citation said no measurement existed below it; this one does). Resolves the prior debt: basin (very_loose_granular dust-pond) modeled at the measured near-surface value; mean corrected 1100->900 (rounded slightly above the exact 850 to reflect a shallow layer rather than the single radar-resolved skin), spread kept at 200 to honestly reflect single-site/single-method uncertainty. Primary DOI paywalled (HTTP 402); corroborated via two independent search syntheses agreeing on identical figures (see matter_library_sources.md, tb-0181 addendum).

appearance.note: the one environment material with real subsurface depth â€” the slab's MFP field earns its keep here. Albedo IS supported (clean ice/snow visible albedo 0.5-0.9 range, search synthesis - matches this entry's ~0.82 mean luminance, unlike sand/rock/metal's magnitude gap). subsurface_mfp_mm (8.0) and translucency (0.35) remain unresolved (tb-0181 follow-up): Warren's 'Optical properties of ice and snow' review (PMC6501920) gives pure ice's ABSORPTION mean free path as 'hundreds of metres' for blue/visible light - real bubble-free ice is nearly non-absorbing at this scale, so 8mm reads as a stylistic SCATTERING choice (bubbles/impurities/frost) rather than a measured constant; no directly-comparable decorative-ice-chunk scattering measurement was found (only non-comparable deep-glacial-ice photon transport, already ruled out by tb-0172). Debt stays provisional, now with stronger physical grounding for why it cannot yet be pinned.
